column1: # Assignments to `$this->` outside the constructor, in every class that is a
# rule. Empty body below the header means zero such assignments.
# WHAT PRODUCED IT: enumeration-execution-state.py — the rule set is built
# TRANSITIVELY (implements RuleInterface, or reaches AbstractRule through any
# chain of parents), then brace matching locates each constructor body and a
# regex finds `$this->prop =` / `.=` / `+=` outside it. 49 rule classes in 49
# files; 0 assignments.
# WHAT IT CANNOT SEE: second-order state — a rule calling a collaborator that
# mutates itself (the known one is InlineDirectivePolicy::enableUsageReporting);
# static properties; state held by configuration validators, which are
# enumerated in enumeration-rule-collaborators.tsv instead; state inside the
# capability preparation services the pipeline primes before execution;
# mutation through a reference or an object the rule merely holds.
# WHY IT MATTERS: it is the STATIC half of the re-entrancy claim, and it is only
# a half — absence of a written property is not proof of a stable outcome. The
# empirical control (two passes, one fingerprint; verdict re-taken on the last
# pass of the sweep) is what proves it. A previous version of this script
# selected rules by a single declaration line and saw 35 of the 49; the numbers
# were the same, the method was not.
